text.p: Knoll Inc, which makes office systems and business furniture, was the most actively traded stock on the New York Stock Exchange Friday after the company's initial public offering.
Shares rose 1/2 to 17 with more than a million shares traded early in the session. The 8 million shares priced lower than their expected price range of $19 to $22.
The cutback means the East Greenville, Pa. company raised about $136 million from the IPO, instead of the $164 million it had hoped for based on the midpoint of the estimated pricing range.
Merrill Lynch was the lead underwriter of the offering. Credit Suisse First Boston, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley also underwriter the IPO.
Chile's third-largest supermarket chain Supermercados Unimarc SA also made its NYSE debut Friday, jumping 1-1/4 to 18 in early trading for a gain of about 7.5 percent.
The American Depositary Receipts(ADRs) sold for $16.75 each to IPO investors, with price talk at $16 to $18. Each of the 4.46 million ADRs is worth 50 shares of common stocks.
Unimarc is the second largest supermarket operator in Chile's capital Santiago, where Unimarc is headquartered.
Unimarc, the second Chilean supermarket to trade on the NYSE, has said it plans to use proceeds to double the number of its stores in the coming years.
Shares of Santa Isabel SA were launched on Wall Street nearly two years ago and another supermarket company, D&S SA, plans to issues ADRs later this year or in early 1998.
Other companies that made their IPO debuts:
-- Shares of Brigham Exploration rose 1/8 to 8-1/8 after the Dallas company's IPO. The company provides exploration services using three-dimensional seismic imaging.
